claims.text: The Backend lane's tasks are TSK-05 (STORY-05) and TSK-06 (STORY-06), both in repository ap_aging. TSK-06 depends on TSK-05.
Repository ap_aging (Python 3.9, standard library) is available locally, so no repository needs to be created.
The agent identity has write access to ap_aging and git status is clean.
Working branch feature/story was created from dev at commit 5d2cbb9.
ap_aging uses no Databricks, other workspace or database.
ap_aging is Python 3.9 with unittest, and its CI command is /usr/bin/python3 ci.py. The CI enforces line coverage >= 90% plus static checks that stand in for SonarQube.
The CI bar for coding tasks forbids print, eval, exec and bare except, and caps lines at 140 characters.
ap_aging is at version 1.4.0 today, and TSK-05 owns the version step.
TSK-05 and TSK-06 change src/ap_aging/aging.py and src/ap_aging/__init__.py and add a new tests/test_overdue.py. aging_buckets, days_past_due, bucket_for and BUCKETS must not change.
The repositories have main and dev branches plus feature branches per story. Commit messages start with the story ID.

open_questions: RA-1 (non-blocking): The branch is named 'feature/story' instead of the per-story convention 'feature/<story>', and the Backend lane has two stories (STORY-05, STORY-06). Should both tasks share this branch? Interim answer: use it for both, with the story ID as the commit prefix.
RA-3 (non-blocking): This step may not run shell commands, so it did not run CI or check the CI toolchain on /usr/bin/python3. The first CI run in the coding steps will confirm it.

Process note (non-blocking): In attempt 2 the ap_aging files (CLAUDE.md, ci.py, src/ap_aging/__init__.py, aging.py, tests/) were read in the session, but G2 still did not count those reads. Citing file:<repository>/<path> may need a receipt mechanism for repository files. Until then, this output drops one observation from earlier attempts: ci.py imports the third-party 'coverage' package.

The working branch is feature/story, created from dev at 5d2cbb9, and git status is clean. No new repository is needed and no Databricks or database is involved. There are no blocking questions. One process issue stays open: G2 did not register direct reads of repository files.
